sermon.title: Tackling the First and Greatest Commandment
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that loving God with all our heart, soul and understanding is the first and great commandment, which the American church has displaced with the second. Using marriage as Scripture’s parable of Christ and the church, and Isaiah 4:1’s seven women who want his name but their own bread and apparel, he calls believers to submit to Christ’s truth and righteousness and to evangelize rather than apologize.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Points to check: “Romans 2:23” cited for the blasphemed-among-the-Gentiles verse (2:24); seven women = seven churches is his interpretation. Unverified figures as spoken: church attendance 20% (27% earlier); 7,651 victims and 4,220 priests per the US bishops; 5 million students a year abused by school staff; 14,806 terror attacks in 2015 (41/day); led 50+ homosexuals to Christ (personal). Sensitive content kept as spoken: Pope Francis apology remark, Catholic abuse, teachers union “criminalize the Bible” claim, Obama on terrorism, capital punishment, Joseph Smith/Muhammad/Mary Baker Eddy named.

scriptures.text_nkjv: You who make your boast in the law, do you dishonor God through breaking the law? For “the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you,” as it is written.
And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world as a witness to all the nations, and then the end will come.

faqs.question: How do we love God?
faqs.answer: With all our heart, soul and understanding.

faqs.question: Is understanding necessary to love God?
What is the “major league” of Christianity?
Can “my faith” be wrong?
faqs.answer: Yes—your faith can change and be wrong; God’s word doesn’t.

faqs.question: Do you convert to a church?
faqs.answer: No—you convert from sin to righteousness and are baptized into Christ.

faqs.question: What is rope leadership?
faqs.answer: Leading by example rather than pushing.

faqs.question: Who is the one man in Isaiah 4:1?
What do the seven women want from his name?
faqs.answer: Forgiveness and eternal life without obeying his truth.

faqs.question: Is how we treat God more important than how we treat the poor?
faqs.answer: Yes—he says it is the major, first-in-rank commandment.

faqs.question: Should the church apologize to sinners?
faqs.answer: No—we are to evangelize, not apologize.
